newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: PRESS DIGEST - South Africa - May 14.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - South Africa - May 14.

text.p: These are the leading stories in the South African press on Wednesday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
BUSINESS DAY

- Deputy President Thabo Mbeki flew out of SA last night for the Congolese port of Pointe Noire for today's make-or-break Zairean peace talks aboard an SA Navy vessel as reports emerged that rebel troops were just 50 km from the Zairean capital, Kinshasa. An unconfirmed report said the rebel vanguard had already reached the city.
- Local authorities that have defaulted on their debts face legal action and the possibility that their assets will be attached, as central government is refusing to bail them out.

- A proposed legislative amendment which will partly lift the veil of secrecy from the Reserve Bank's activities was sent back for redrafting by the parliamentary finance committee on Tuesday because it did not go far enough in achieving transparency.
- The African National Congress (ANC) has lost control of township self-defence units, Deputy President Thabo Mbeki admitted to the truth commission on Tuesday.
- A deal for the sale of Transtel Cellular to cellular provider MTN was imminent, Transtel Cellular CE Thero Setiloane said on Tuesday.
BUSINESS REPORT

- The Reserve Bank is planning to act to stem the relentless growth in the use of home loans to finance consumer spending, Christo Wiese, the registrar of banks, said in the Bank's annual report tabled in parliament on Tuesday.

- Daewoo DWGR.CN, the $76 billion a year Korean multinational is investigating investment opportunities worth nearly $360 million in South Africa over the next few years, Byung-Ju Chang, the executive vice president of Daewoo, said on Tuesday.

- Weak performances from its non-beverage interests and a 74 million rand loss at OK Bazaars took the sparkle out of the performance of South African Breweries, the brewing and industrial conglomerate.

- Rebhold, the recently listed food, freight and liquor company, has concluded a 160 million rand deal with the Mineworkers' Investment Company (MIC), the empowerment initiative of the National Union of Mineworkers, the companies said on Tuesday.

- The more police forces around the world became overloaded fighting violent crime, the more the private sector would to have to step into the breach to fight commerical, white-collar crime, William Sessions, a former firector of the FBI, said on Tuesday.
SAKE BEELD
- The result of SA Brewries (SAB) for the year to March was weaker than expected after the price increase by 325c to R130.
- OK Bazaars recorded a loss of 74 million rand in the year to March, whereas the loss in the previous year was 1 million rand.
- Although the loss at Rainbow Chicken grew this year to 60.5 cents per ordinary share, from 43.4 cents in the previous financial year, a considerable advance can be identified.
THE STAR

- ANC Women's League's deputy president Thandi Modise was threatened with death at the organisation's national congress last month if she did not withdraw from the race with Winnie Madikizela-Mandela for the league's presidency.

- Mdu was only 10 when he witnessed the murder of his grandmother and a brutal attack on his grandfather. Now 16, he says he wants to put that behind him - pick up the pieces of his life - and go back to school, where he hasn't been for six years.
- High school pupils visiting the Gauteng legislature on Tuesday were treated to a display of name-calling and insult trading which speaker Trevor Fowler described as a shambles.
- Police have made a break through in their investigations into the rape of a nine-months pregnant Blairgowrie, Randburg, woman and her 24 year old sister with the arrest of two suspects.
